docs.title: 🧠 Welcome to the PyGen Documentation
docs.text:
PyGen is an internal library developed to standardize and accelerate data engineering and machine learning processes within Genesis.

This portal was built with MkDocs + Material for MkDocs, and serves as the official reference for the library’s resources.

docs.title: ✨ Main Features
docs.text:
• 📦 Custom SparkSession for local, cloud, and Databricks environments
  • 🧠 AutoLogMixin: automatic logging of method calls
  • 📊 Base FeatureEngineering class with validated data reading (Delta/Parquet)
  • 🔄 Future integrations with MLflow, Airflow, and more

docs.title: 📄 Documentation Structure
docs.text:
• Logger: How to use the logger with colors, context, and levels.
  • SparkSession: Initialization of portable Spark sessions.
  • FeatureEngineering: Base class for data transformation.

docs.title: 🤝 How to Contribute
docs.text: You can contribute to the documentation collaboratively! Simply visit the Docs Contributing section and follow the recommended steps!

docs.title: 📚 About the PyGen Documentation
docs.text: This documentation portal was built with MkDocs using the Material theme, with the goal of organizing, standardizing, and facilitating the use of the resources provided by the PyGen library.

docs.title: ✨ Objectives
docs.text:
• Document the main components of the library (loggers, mixins, sessions, etc.)
  • Serve as a quick reference for those using or integrating PyGen
  • Make knowledge easily accessible for data engineering and machine learning teams

docs.title: ✍️ How to Contribute
docs.text:
1. Check out the repository and create a new branch: bash git checkout -b docs/improvement-example

  2. Edit or create .md files inside the /docs folder.

  3. Preview locally: bash mkdocs serve

  4. Build the final version: bash mkdocs build

  5. Submit your PR with the documented changes.

docs.title: 💡 Best Practices
docs.text:
• Use clear and concise language
  • Always include examples when possible
  • Update the navigation in mkdocs.yml when adding new pages

docs.title: 🧠 FeatureEngineering Base Class
docs.text: FeatureEngineering is a foundational class for managing data loading, transformation logic, and reuse across feature pipelines. It extends AutoLogMixin for automatic logging and includes a ready-to-use SparkSession.

docs.title: 🔧 Features
docs.text:
• Auto-managed SparkSession
  • Safe and validated dataset loading
  • Format support: Delta, Parquet
  • Layered path abstraction (e.g., bronze/silver/gold)
  • Logging of entry/exit and exceptions via AutoLogMixin

docs.title: 🧱 Initialization
docs.text:
from pygen.core.engineering.feature_engineering import FeatureEngineering

query = """
    SELECT 
        id,
        name,
        age
    FROM 
        customers.accounts.profile
""" 

class MyFeature(FeatureEngineering):
    def __init__():
        super().__init__()

    def process():
        df = self.load_table("customers", layer="silver")
        query_df = self.run_query(query)

        return df.join(query, on="id", how="inner")

docs.title: load_table(table: str, layer: Optional[str] = None, format: str = "delta")
docs.text: Loads a dataset by combining the layer and table path, and validates supported formats.

docs.title: run_query(query: str)
docs.text: Loads data using SQL query and return a spark dataframe.

docs.title: _read_data(path: str, format: str = "delta")
docs.text: Internal method for direct path-based reading with validation and error handling.

docs.title: ⚠️ Error Handling
docs.text:
• Raises ValueError for unsupported formats.
  • Raises RuntimeError with descriptive message if dataset can't be read.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Logger module provides a standardized and enhanced logging system with: - Colored log levels for better visibility in terminal outputs. - Contextual logging that includes the logger name. - Automatic logging of method calls (entry, exit, errors) via the AutoLogMixin.

This utility is ideal for logging in both data engineering and machine learning pipelines with minimal boilerplate.

docs.title: ✨ Features
docs.text:
• ANSI-colored logs for better readability in CLI environments.
  • Automatic logging of public method calls (AutoLogMixin) — no need to manually decorate methods.
  • Safe and extensible architecture using Python’s logging, inspect, and functools libraries.

docs.title: Logger class
docs.text: logger = Logger(name="MyService", level="DEBUG").get()

docs.title: Parameters:
docs.text: Parameter Type Description name str Logger name shown in log messages level str Logging level (DEBUG, INFO, etc.)

docs.title: Methods:
docs.text: • get() – Returns the configured logging.Logger instance.

docs.title: Output Format:
docs.text: [2025-04-23 12:00:00] [DEBUG] [MyService] - Message here

docs.title: ColoredFormatter class
docs.text: A custom formatter that injects ANSI escape codes to color the log level names.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
• DEBUG: Blue
  • INFO: Green
  • WARNING: Yellow
  • ERROR: Red
  • CRITICAL: Magenta

docs.title: auto_log(logger) function
docs.text: A decorator factory that returns a decorator which: - Logs method/function entry (with arguments) - Logs return value on exit - Logs exceptions and stack traces if an error occurs

docs.title: Usage:
docs.text:
@auto_log(logger)
def my_function(x, y):
    return x + y

docs.title: AutoLogMixin class
docs.text: A mixin that automatically applies the auto_log decorator to all public instance methods of a class that has a self.logger attribute.

docs.title: Usage:
docs.text:
class MyComponent(AutoLogMixin):
    def __init__(self):
        self.logger = Logger("MyComponent", "DEBUG").get()
        super().__init__()

    def process(self, data):
        return [d * 2 for d in data]

docs.title: Behavior:
docs.text:
• Automatically wraps all methods that:
  • Don’t start with _
  • Are callable
  • Are instance-bound methods (not static or class methods)

docs.title: ✅ Output (with colors):
docs.text:
[2025-04-23 12:00:00] [DEBUG] [MyComponent] - Entering: process | args=(...), kwargs={}
[2025-04-23 12:00:00] [DEBUG] [MyComponent] - Exiting: process | return=[...]

docs.title: 💡 Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always call super().__init__() when using AutoLogMixin.
  • Use descriptive logger names (e.g., ETLStep1, ModelTrainer) for traceability.

docs.title: 📎 Example Full Usage
docs.text:
class MyService(AutoLogMixin):
    def __init__(self):
        self.logger = Logger("MyService", "DEBUG").get()
        super().__init__()

    def add(self, a, b):
        return a + b

s = MyService()
s.add(2, 3)

docs.title: 🚀 PyGen SparkSession
docs.text: The SparkSession class is a standardized and portable wrapper around pyspark.sql.SparkSession, designed to simplify and unify the Spark initialization process across local, cloud, and Databricks environments.

docs.title: ✨ Features
docs.text:
• Loads external YAML configs
  • Custom tags for observability (e.g., lineage, team, env)
  • Predefined defaults for shuffle partitions and timezone
  • Compatible with Delta Lake, Parquet, and more
  • Logging with contextual info

docs.title: 🧱 Initialization
docs.text:
from pygen.infra.service.spark.spark_session import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession(
    app_name="MyApp",
    tags={"env": "dev", "owner": "ds-team"}
)
df = spark.read.parquet("path/to/file.parquet")

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuration
docs.text:
• If configs/spark_defaults.yaml exists, it's automatically loaded.
  • You can override configs using the tags, app_name, or YAML file.
  • Tags are added as spark.genesis.tag.{key} Spark properties.

docs.title: 📤 Output Example (logs)
docs.text:
[INFO] SparkSession initialized - App: MyApp
[INFO] Spark version: 3.x.x
[INFO] Applied tags: {'env': 'dev', 'owner': 'ds-team'}
